name: Assassination
overview: The Bible clearly condemns assassination as a grievous sin, emphasizing the commandment 'Thou shalt not kill' (Exodus 20:13) and pronouncing curses on those who secretly slay or accept bribes to kill the innocent (Deuteronomy 27:24-25). Instances of assassination, such as Ehud's killing of Eglon (Judges 3:15,20) and the sons of Rimmon killing Ish-bosheth (2 Samuel 4:9), illustrate the gravity and complexity of such acts within Israel's history. David's abhorrence of assassination further highlights the sacredness of life and the divine judgment against covert murder.
